item.text: {"case_id":"SHC057","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C18","C23","C25"],"selected_candidate_label":"C18","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C18 plausibly supplied a concrete core template for the later Libya order. Both use nearly identical emergency findings, then prohibit imports, exports, and transportation involving the targeted country, delegate implementation to Treasury, prescribe a precise delayed effective time, and require transmission to Congress and publication in the Federal Register. The Libya order substantially expands this machinery with financial, contractual, travel, and anti-evasion provisions resembling C23 and C25, but C18 provides the strongest overall drafting skeleton.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"find that the policies and actions of the Government of Libya constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States and hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat","parent_excerpt":"find that the policies and actions of the Government of Nicaragua constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy of the United States and hereby declare a national emergency to deal with that threat","explanation":"Distinctive near-verbatim emergency finding with only the target country changed."},{"child_excerpt":"The import into the United States of any goods or services of Libyan origin; ... The export to Libya of any goods, technology ... or services from the United States","parent_excerpt":"all imports into the United States of goods and services of Nicaraguan origin; all exports from the United States of goods to or destined for Nicaragua","explanation":"Parallel paired import-and-export embargo provisions adapted from Nicaragua to Libya and elaborated with exceptions."},{"child_excerpt":"Any transaction by a United States person relating to transportation to or from Libya; the provision of transportation ... by any Libyan person or any vessel or aircraft of Libyan registration","parent_excerpt":"prohibit Nicaraguan air carriers from engaging in air transportation to or from points in the United States ... prohibit vessels of Nicaraguan registry from entering into United States ports","explanation":"The later order broadens the same air-and-vessel transportation restrictions into a more comprehensive transportation clause."},{"child_excerpt":"The Secretary of the Treasury ... is hereby authorized to take such actions ... as may be necessary to carry out the purposes of this Order","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of the Treasury is delegated and authorized to employ all powers granted to me ... to carry out the purposes of this Order","explanation":"Closely parallel Treasury implementation machinery following the substantive prohibitions."},{"child_excerpt":"shall apply as of 12:01 a.m. Eastern Standard Time, February 1, 1986 ... transmitted to the Congress and published in the Federal Register","parent_excerpt":"shall be effective as of 12:01 a.m., Eastern Daylight Time, May 7, 1985, and shall be transmitted to the Congress and published in the Federal Register","explanation":"Same concluding sequence of a precisely timed effective date followed by congressional transmission and Federal Register publication."}]}
